Furtive

FUR-tiv -- from Latin furtivus ('stolen, secret'), from furtum ('theft'). · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Furtive is secretive or sly, typically because of guilt or fear of being caught.

During the exam, the proctor noticed a furtive exchange of glances between two students seated in the back row.

Worked Example

At the family dinner, the twins exchanged furtive smirks every time their grandmother mentioned the missing pie.

Notice furtive almost always describes small physical behaviors -- a glance, a movement, a whisper -- that betray guilt or the wish not to be noticed, not a general personality trait.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

stealthy: moving or acting carefully to avoid being seen or heard

surreptitious: done secretly, often to avoid being caught

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

open: done publicly, with nothing hidden

forthright: direct and straightforward, without hiding anything

Where it sits · how guilty and deliberate the secrecy is — stealthy → furtive → surreptitious

stealthy vs. furtive: Stealthy is milder than furtive: a cat creeping along a fence is merely quiet and careful, while furtive adds a sharper edge of guilt and fear of being caught.

surreptitious vs. furtive: Surreptitious is stronger than furtive: a furtive glance betrays nervous secrecy for a moment, but surreptitiously photographing a confidential memo is deliberate, fully concealed wrongdoing.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — furt-

root — furt-: theft, something stolen (Latin (furtum))

suffix — -ive

suffix — -ive: having the nature or quality of (Latin (-ivus))

Put it together

Put it together: Furtive comes from the Latin word for theft -- so someone acting furtive is, at the root, acting the way a thief would: quick, quiet, and careful not to be seen.

Use the root in a new word: furtively

Use the root in a new word: furtively: He furtively slipped the extra cookie into his pocket when he thought no one was looking.

Word Building

Word Choice

Furtive describes small guilty-looking behaviors -- glances, movements, whispers -- not a whole secret operation. Compare Clandestine, which describes an entire activity or meeting kept secret and usually forbidden. A person can give a furtive glance during a perfectly legal meeting; a clandestine meeting is the secret event itself.
